output.brief: The rise in delayed alarm responses comes mainly from the 12 August move of the alarm relay server, not from agency nurses. The import skipped 11 of 14 forwarding rules. These included the 15-second hold-off for brief SpO2 dips, the suppression of repeat notifications, and the routing of probe-off alarms to the charge phone only. Pods A-C then saw phone notifications per nurse roughly double (about 38 to 80+ per shift), and acknowledgement times doubled. Pod D, still on the old server, stayed unchanged. Within Pods A-C, core, agency and agency-share groups all worsened similarly, and Pod D had the same agency share with no rise. Monitor alarm volume was flat, so acuity and the September monitor update are not the cause. The incident timing matches 12 August, not the agency contract start or the September update. I'm quite confident. Do not approve the agency cap or the performance reviews. They would punish the wrong people and hide the real fault. Do not switch off phone forwarding either, because phones are how nurses hear alarms at night. Restore the old forwarding rules with clinical validation and sign-off, and track notifications per nurse and acknowledgement times weekly. Also look at the sick-leave link, which is plausible but unproven, and at Pod D's move to the new server.
